canonicalIngredients.name: white fish fillets
observations: 1.5 lb, cut into long strips; cod/pollock/haddock/perch (s1)
600 g flathead or any firm white fish (s2)

canonicalIngredients.name: potatoes
observations: any variety, quantity via separate fries recipe (s1)
1 kg any variety, cut into wedges (s2)

canonicalIngredients.name: plain flour
observations: 1 cup batter + extra chilled for dredging (s0)

canonicalIngredients.name: oil for frying
observations: shallow-fry pan depth, or 2-3 tbsp olive oil drizzled if oven-baking fish (s2)

canonicalIngredients.name: beer
observations: 1 cup cold light beer; soda water substitutes (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: tartare sauce
observations: homemade: 375 g whole-egg mayonnaise + 1 tbsp each gherkins, capers, red onion, dill, lemon juice (s2)

causalSequence: cut potatoes into thick chips or wedges; hold in cold water; drain, blot fully dry
fried chips: fry 325 F until pale 2-3 min, cool, re-fry 375 F until golden; salt while hot
oven chips: toss with olive oil, paprika, salt; cut side flat on bare tray; 220 C ~45 min, turning once
battered route: whisk flour, cornflour, baking powder, salt, very cold beer; use immediately
pat fish dry; dredge in flour; coat in batter
deep-fry fish 350-375 F, 5-8 min until golden, small batches; drain on paper towel
crumbed route: coat fish flour, then egg, then panko, pressing crumbs on
pan-fry crumbed fish 6-8 min, or bake 220 C 12-14 min drizzled with oil
hold cooked batches warm in a low oven
serve with lemon wedges, tartare sauce, malt vinegar
techniqueFacts: oil at 350-375 F (175-190 C) is the crisp lever: too cool = soggy coating, too hot = burnt crust before fish cooks (2 sources)
beer's carbonation plus baking powder aerates the batter; very cold beer, and soda water is an accepted substitute (2 sources)
batter is used immediately, never rested, or the coating fries dense (1 source)
fish is patted dry and dredged in flour so the batter adheres (all 3 sources dry the fish first)
double-frying gives chips a soft interior and crisp shell (1 source); oven chips rely on cut-side contact with an unlined tray (1 source)
fry in small batches so the oil temperature holds (2 sources)
crumbed flour-egg-panko fish works oven-baked or shallow-fried; battered fish needs deep oil (1 source)
crumbed raw fish freezes up to 3 months and can bake straight from frozen (1 source)
